entries.name: Norway lemming
entries.migrates: mass downhill movements in boom years ('lemming runs')

breeding.season: all summer, multiple litters in boom years

behaviour: dense black-brown dorsal stripe over rufous flanks; turns orange-brown in summer
boom-crash cycle; in peak years densities carpet the open tundra
digs shallow runways under the snow to feed in winter

voxel_model.pattern: dark dorsal stripe on rufous flanks

entries.notes: The lemming of the famous runs down Scandinavian mountainsides; the entire predator guild above it starves when the cycle troughs. Four-year cycle, like its American cousins.

entries.name: Root vole (tundra vole)
behaviour: the most widespread vole of the wet sedge tundra
eats cotton grass roots and rhizomes through the winter under the snow
runways through thick sedge are visible from above on dry years

voxel_model.pattern: uniform dark brown, short tail

entries.notes: Circumpolar and easy to overlook, but wet-tundra biomass runs through this vole; the default prey for tundra owls in much of Eurasia.

entries.name: Siberian lemming
entries.migrates: mass movements in boom years across the Yamal and Taymyr

breeding.season: all summer, multiple litters in boom years

behaviour: larger and darker than the Norway lemming; the rodent at the heart of the Siberian boom-crash cycle
runs in dense waves across the open Yamal tundra, devouring cottongrass mat
dens under deep snow keep feeding in midwinter

voxel_model.pattern: dark brown back over rufous-flanked sides

entries.notes: The lemming of the great Siberian runs — the species behind the pomarine jaeger's Arctic irruptions. Distinct from the Norway lemming; both were once placed together in Lemmus.

entries.name: Horned lark (shorelark)
entries.migrates: breeds on open Arctic and alpine ground; short migrations to open temperate country
behaviour: the only true lark of the open Arctic
male gives a sweet, tinkling song in display flight from a rock or hummock
builds a grass-lined scrape on bare moss or gravel

voxel_model.pattern: black breast band and black 'horns' against a sandy back

entries.notes: The bird of the desolate gravel ridge and fell field; its song is the small comfort of the high tundra. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Common redpoll
entries.migrates: nomadic winter wanderer; irrupts south in poor seed years
behaviour: crimson poll and bib against a frosted, streaked body
rolls birch seeds in a pouch in its bill to crack and discard the husk
flocks work weedy and birch ground in chattering waves

voxel_model.pattern: streaked flanks, crimson forehead and bib, yellow bill

entries.notes: A finch you hear before you see; in lean years the dark-bibbed males gather at any weed seed near the camp. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Hoary redpoll
entries.migrates: irruptive; follows seed crops and drifts out of the High Arctic in winter
behaviour: paler and frostier than the common redpoll, with a stubbier, deeper bill
the true High Arctic redpoll; breeds right up to the polar sea
often mixed into common redpoll flocks in winter
sounds: soft twitters, a shade thinner than common redpoll's

voxel_model.pattern: frosty pale body, little flank streaking, crimson poll

entries.notes: Splitter's delight: told from common redpoll by the smaller bill and whiter body; treat ranges with care since the two mix freely. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Northern wheatear
entries.migrates: breeds across the Arctic; winters in sub-Saharan Africa, one of the great migration fliers
behaviour: stands upright on a boulder flashing a white rump and black terminal tail band
bobs and quivers the tail while perched
fortress nest in a deep rock crevice or burrow
sounds: chatty whistling calls and a hard chatter

voxel_model.pattern: grey back, black facial mask (male), white rump over black tail band

entries.notes: A flycatcher-wheatear that migrates from the Arctic circle to tropical Africa in about two weeks, and back again in spring — one of the longest yearly commutes of any songbird. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Red-throated pipit
entries.migrates: breeds across the treeless Arctic; winters in southern Asia and Africa
behaviour: russet-washed throat and face in breeding dress
walks steadily on the ground between picks, never darts like a wheatear
nests as a loose colony in wet tundra
sounds: thin descending song similar to a parakeet's chatter

voxel_model.pattern: heavily streaked breast, rusty throat flush

entries.notes: A thrush-sized streaky dart over wet tundra; the Eurasian counterpart of the American sparrow-songs. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: American golden plover
entries.migrates: breeds Arctic North America; winters on the pampas of southern South America, one of the longest land migrations on Earth
behaviour: breeding male is gold-spangled above with a jet-black face and belly
long southbound flight of some 15,000 km from the Arctic to Argentina
migrates with shoreline staging at immense autumn flocks

voxel_model.pattern: gold-spangled back, black belly and face with white flank line

entries.notes: One of the great migrants: the whole North American population passes over the midcontinent in a few weeks each autumn. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Eurasian golden plover
entries.migrates: breeds on Arctic tundra and moorland; winters on farmland and coasts of western Europe and the Mediterranean
behaviour: breeding male is black below with a golden-epauletted back
haunting, fluty three-note whistle over the moor
winters in vast flocks on stubble fields
sounds: fluty poo-eee calls; a melancholy, descending whistle

voxel_model.pattern: black face and underparts, golden-spotted mantle

entries.notes: The sound of the moorland ptarmigan country; in winter the great flocks wheeling over stubble are a farmer-country spectacle. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Black-bellied plover
entries.migrates: breeds on high Arctic tundra; winters on coasts nearly worldwide
behaviour: the boldest and biggest of the high-Arctic plovers; black belly sets off the white rump
finds winter on tropical coasts, feeding by feel with a ploughing bill
both sexes share incubation

voxel_model.pattern: black face and belly, silver-spangled grey back, white rump in flight

entries.notes: A plover with a bigger bill than it strictly needs — it forages by touch at night on migration. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Semipalmated sandpiper
entries.migrates: breeds Arctic North America; winters on South American coasts, staging in immense Delaware Bay numbers
behaviour: one of the smallest Arctic sandpipers; half-webbed toes
doubled body weight on Delaware Bay horseshoe-crab eggs fuels the nonstop Atlantic crossing
nests in a shallow scrape among hummocks

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown above, white below, black legs

entries.notes: A sandpiper eclipsed in sheer numbers only by the dunlin; its fate hangs on one Delaware Bay stopover each spring. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Dunlin
entries.migrates: breeds circumpolar Arctic tundra; winters on temperate mudflats
behaviour: breeding adult carries a rusty mantle and bold black belly patch
winter flocks feed in shimmering tideline stitching at mudflats
deceptively rotund in breeding dress; marathon migrant

voxel_model.pattern: rufous-rust mantle, black belly and decurved bill in breeding dress

entries.notes: The small shorebird most people actually notice on an autumn mudflat; a classic 'peep' with a slightly droopy bill. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Whimbrel
entries.migrates: breeds on open Arctic tundra; winters on tropical coasts, often in flocks of hundreds
behaviour: long downcurved bill and a bold striped crown
bubbling glissando whistle, accelerating down the scale
robs gull and tern nests when it can

voxel_model.pattern: long decurved bill, bold head stripes, mottled brown

entries.notes: A curlew-shaped migrant that talks nonstop on the coast; on the tundra it sings from the wing over its nesting hummock. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Ruff
entries.migrates: breeds on wet Eurasian tundra and marsh; winters on African and southern wetlands

breeding.season: spring to midsummer; lekking, female incubates alone

behaviour: breeding males explode into a ruff of erectile neck feathers, each male radiantly different
males gather at traditional leks and posture, flutter and fight for females
females are plain sedge-coloured and leave the male behind after mating
sounds: mostly silent at the lek; soft calls away from it

voxel_model.pattern: variable: black, chestnut, white or rufous ruffs on different males

entries.notes: A shorebird the size of a thrush with a turkey-cock attitude; the feathered ruff and tufted head of each male are genetically unique. gestation_days is incubation time; clutch about 3-4 eggs.

entries.name: Red-necked phalarope
entries.migrates: breeds on Arctic tundra pools; winters far out at sea in tropical oceans
behaviour: role reversal echoing the red phalarope: bright female, duller incubating male
swims in tight circles to spin up tiny vortices and vacuum in plankton
fully pelagic in winter, farther from land than almost any shorebird

voxel_model.pattern: grey above, chestnut neck (female), white underparts

entries.notes: The subarctic sibling of the red phalarope; together they account for nearly every phalarope the player will ever see. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Pomarine jaeger
entries.migrates: breeds on coastal Arctic tundra; winters on tropical oceans worldwide

breeding.season: summer, only in lemming boom years

behaviour: the largest of the three jaegers, with long twisted spoon-shaped central tail feathers
breeds only when lemmings are abundant; may skip years entirely or move hundreds of kilometres
in a good year the tundra is dotted with its nests near the coast

voxel_model.pattern: pale and dark morphs; dark cap, twisted spoon tail streamers

entries.notes: More than 90 percent of breeding-season prey is lemmings; the best clue to a boom year is a big jaeger standing over the sedge. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Long-tailed jaeger
entries.migrates: breeds on high Arctic tundra; winters entirely at sea, especially the south Atlantic and Indian oceans
behaviour: the smallest, most graceful jaeger; impossibly long thin tail streamers
hovers kitelike into a headwind, then drops onto lemmings and voles
often nests further inland and higher than other jaegers

voxel_model.pattern: dark cap; very long central tail streamers in breeding adults

entries.notes: The kestrel-like jaeger: hangs on the wind like an American kestrel over the open sedge, then pounces. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Peregrine falcon (tundrius)
entries.migrates: breeds on Arctic cliffs; winters across temperate and tropical coasts

breeding.season: spring to early summer, on coastal cliff ledges

behaviour: the fastest animal on Earth in a stoop; over 300 km/h on a stooped dive
takes shorebirds on the wing with a single hammering strike
defends towering cliff territories, often near tern colonies

voxel_model.pattern: slate back, barred white underparts, bold black moustache

entries.notes: The most widespread raptor on Earth, and on the coast it patrols the tern colonies like a cat outside a bakery. gestation_days is incubation time; tundrius is the small, pale Arctic subspecies.

entries.name: Merlin
entries.migrates: breeds on open Arctic and boreal ground; winters on coasts and farmland to the south
behaviour: a small dark falcon that chases songbirds to the ground in sprints
typically glides low over the sedge rather than stooping from height
famously bold at defending its nest; drives off much larger raptors

voxel_model.pattern: dark slate above, streaked below, single dark tail bar

entries.notes: The poor man's peregrine; it lives entirely off songbirds it catches in level, flat-out sprints. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Short-eared owl
entries.migrates: nomadic; drifts to areas with rodent peaks, often with several pairs per valley

breeding.season: spring and summer, timed to vole abundance

behaviour: hunts open ground by day, quartering low like a harrier
booms and claps during a spectacular sky-dance courtship in spring dusk
nest is a scrape hidden in rank grass or sedge

voxel_model.pattern: tawny streaked back, black wrist patches under the wing, yellow eyes

entries.notes: The only owl the player will see in broad daylight over open country; the other lemming owl to the snowy's white. gestation_days is incubation time.

entries.name: Narrow-skulled vole
behaviour: strictly colonial; dozens of burrows threaded under a single turf hummock
the dominant vole of the Eurasian high tundra, from Yamal to the Bering Sea
keeps active all winter in tunnels under the snow

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown above, pale below

entries.notes: The vole that carpets the Eurasian tundra; where it lives, the snowy owl and short-eared owl breed in numbers. Now often placed in Lasiopodomys.

entries.name: Grey red-backed vole
behaviour: reddish-chestnut back with grey flanks, the taiga's signpost vole
gathers berries and lichen in runways at the tundra fringe
population cycle less violent than the lemmings but still bumpy

voxel_model.pattern: brick-red back over grey flanks

entries.notes: A vole of the willow-birch scrub at the tundra's edge; the Eurasian answer to the bank voles further south.

entries.name: Tundra shrew
behaviour: the truest-Arctic shrew; the only shrew of the high Siberian tundra
heart races at over 800 beats per minute; starves within hours if it does not feed
hunts under the snow-sedge mat in tunnels shared with voles

voxel_model.pattern: dark brown back, pale belly, long needle snout

entries.notes: An unstoppable, hypothermic hunger on legs; it eats several times its own weight a day or dies. More easily noticed by its rustling in the leaf litter than seen.

entries.name: Masked shrew
behaviour: the commonest shrew of Alaska and Canada; it reaches the tundra edge
pale eye-ring mask against grey-brown fur
known to produce ultrasonic twittering echolocation pulses

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown back, pale flanks, masked face

entries.notes: The default shrew across most of Alaska; where the sedge is thick it carries the food web's bottom rung for weasels and owls. Barely a mouse in mass.

entries.name: Northern bog lemming
behaviour: cuts square pieces of grass leaves and bolts them into little stacks; the only pika-like haying rodent of the cold
blunt, grooved upper incisors, its field mark if spotted
wet meadows and bog edges rather than open gravel

voxel_model.pattern: dark grey-brown, stouter than a vole

entries.notes: The haymaker of the small rodent world: it clips grass and stacks it like tiny firewood — easy to miss, lovely to find. Its Synaptomys kin were once all in Lemmus.

entries.name: Arctic grayling
entries.migrates: runs up tundra rivers in spring to spawn
behaviour: a huge sail-like dorsal fin, spotted with crimson
rises for caddis and stoneflies in clear streams like a trout
prefers cold, clean northern water; a sentinel of Arctic river health

voxel_model.pattern: high spotted dorsal sail, silvery flanks with faint spots

entries.notes: The Arctic's own trout; the high 'sail' of an adult is unmistakable rising under the midnight sun. gestation_days is null; eggs hatch weeks after the spring spawn.

entries.name: Ninespine stickleback

breeding.season: early summer; male builds and guards a plant nest

behaviour: spines along the back where other sticklebacks have three
males turn black in courtship and guard the egg nest ferociously
thrives in brackish and fresh tundra pools other fish cannot

voxel_model.pattern: small, slim body; nine needle dorsal spines

entries.notes: Small, spiny and everywhere in northern pools; a keystone snack for Arctic char and young phalaropes. gestation_days is null; the male fans the nest with his tail for two weeks.

entries.name: Three-spined stickleback

breeding.season: early summer; male builds and guards a woven nest

behaviour: three dorsal spines lock rigid against predators
breeding males turn bright red-throated with blue eyes
one of the most-studied fish on Earth for behaviour and evolution

voxel_model.pattern: silver sides, red throat and blue eyes in breeding males

entries.notes: The textbook 'red-bellied little bully' of northern streams; the three spines and the male's red throat are the field marks. gestation_days is null; males guard and fan the nest.

entries.name: Eurasian minnow
behaviour: schools of hundreds in cold gravelly tundra streams
breeding males flush crimson along the belly and fins
the canonical live-bait fish of Eurasian taiga and tundra anglers

voxel_model.pattern: olive back, scarlet belly and fins in breeding males

entries.notes: Europe's little river trout-bait; it also happens to be excellent for studying schooling. gestation_days is null; eggs scatter over gravel in spring.

entries.name: Wood frog

breeding.season: days after the spring thaw, in meltwater pools

behaviour: the Arctic's amphibian edge-of-range marvel: freezes solid in winter, heart and breath stopped, then thaws and hops in spring
floods breeding ponds for a frantic few days of quacking chorus
dark mask through the eye is the field mark

voxel_model.pattern: tan-brown body, bold dark eye mask

entries.player: not interactable; too small to bother
entries.notes: A frog that vitrifies its own cells with glucose and survives being frozen for months; at the tundra edge it is the only amphibian that answers the spring thaw. gestation_days is null; tadpoles must beat the pond drying.

entries.name: Arctic tadpole shrimp

breeding.season: one generation per year; eggs overwinter frozen or dry

behaviour: a living fossil; unchanged in body plan for over 200 million years
eggs survive freezing and desiccation for decades; ephemeral pools hatch whole new worlds in a wet year
cannibalistic when crowded; sole large life in fishless High Arctic pools

voxel_model.pattern: flat horseshoe carapace; marbled or monochrome morphs

entries.notes: Turn over a dry stone by a High Arctic meltwater pool and 250 million years of crustacean stares back. Stenothermal — it will fail fast if the pond warms past its narrow optimum near 10 °C.

entries.name: Snow flea (snow springtail)

breeding.season: spring thaw; multiple generations a year

behaviour: swarms on melting snow in dark pepper-like patches on sunny days
glycine-rich antifreeze lets it walk on snow in subzero air
springs away on a furcula like a microscopic flea; hence the name — it is not a flea, nor strictly an insect

voxel_model.pattern: blue-black dots sprinkled on snow

entries.notes: The pepper on the snowmelt. A designer should treat huge dark flecks on sunny spring snowbanks as living springtails; they are a Collembola, their own class, not true insects.

entries.name: Snow midge (glacier midge)

breeding.season: brief summer flights on snowfields and glacier margins

behaviour: the pioneer insect of brand-new glacial meltwater streams
adults mate on snow and ice in shoulder season, barely surviving a warm hand
larvae live in the torrents running off glaciers where nothing else can

voxel_model.pattern: small dark non-biting midge

entries.notes: A midge of melting ice, not blood meals; Chironomidae adults do not feed. The genus Diamesa is the signature life at the nose of every retreating glacier.

entries.name: Arctic fritillary

breeding.season: July flight; larvae may take two years in the High Arctic

behaviour: flies low and fast over dry tundra in a short July window
caterpillars feed on violets, dwarf willows and Cassiope, and hibernate twice in the Arctic
Holarctic; the signature fritillary of the true north

voxel_model.pattern: orange wings with dark spots and dark borders

entries.notes: One of the very few butterflies of the treeless Arctic; newly hatched caterpillars hibernate, fourth-stage caterpillars hibernate again, so a butterfly you meet may have started as an egg two summers ago.

entries.name: Water flea (Daphnia)

breeding.season: all summer; parthenogenetic, with resting eggs over winter

behaviour: swarms turn tundra meltwater pools faintly pink in high summer
reproduces without males most of the year; winter eggs survive the ice
the engine of High Arctic pond food webs: phalaropes, sticklebacks and char all run on it

voxel_model.pattern: tiny translucent shrimp-like specks, often pink

entries.notes: Microscopic, translucent, ubiquitous: this crustacean turns green Arctic pond-water into phalarope and stickleback chicks. Model as a faint pink dust on the water, nothing more.
